chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The merit of the violet (oil) over the (other) oils is like the merit of Islam over the religions. The best of the oils is the violet (oil), for it removes the illness from the head and the two eyes, so anoint yourselves with it.

key_terms.الْأَدْهَانِ: Oils (plural of dahn, referring to massage or anointing oils)
key_terms.الْبَنَفْسَجِ: Violet (specifically referring to the oil extracted from it)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and medicinal significance of violet oil in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), employing the famous rhetorical device of 'tashbih' (analogy) to elevate the status of violet oil (banafsj) as a premier medicinal substance, paralleling its excellence to Islam's supremacy among all religions. This comparison underscores both its spiritual metaphorical weight and its practical efficacy in treating head and eye ailments, reflecting the Shia tradition's emphasis on the healing properties of natural substances blessed by the Imams.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Abdul Rahman Bin Kaseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The merit of the violet (oil) upon the (massaging) oils is like the merit of Al-Islam upon the (rest of the) religions. The best of the (massaging) oils is the violet (oil) for removing the illnesses from the head, and the eyes, therefore oil (massage) with it’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu from Ali ibn Hassan from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The excellence of viola oil over other oils is like the excellence of Islam over other religions. Viola is very good; it banishes the pain from the head and eyes, so you must apply it.’”
